response.internal_assessment: Patricia is no longer the CEO running a corporate structure above me. She is now an owner-operator, which means the org chart just flattened in a way I did not expect. The people she laid off — some of them possibly people my father knew when he ran the original lot — that is on her, but I am the GM who managed those people day to day. That weight belongs to me too. The sector revenue index at 79 tells me what I already know: the showroom floor is bleeding and only the service lane is holding. Savings have dropped two ticks in a row. My monthly expenses are running over income by almost $2,000. I have 4 dependents and 10 months of runway. I am not in crisis but I can see crisis from here. Jake wants a one-on-one — that meeting needs to happen. He is my best remaining floor producer and he is smart enough to be presenting data rather than complaints. The stay bonus he mentioned is the first I have heard of a $12k figure. I do not know if that came from Patricia or whether it is still live given the restructuring. I need to surface that question. Angela's transition map is almost done. When it lands, every person on my floor will be categorized. I need to be the one who helps shape what happens next, not the one who finds out after.
response.inbox_interpretation: Three signal threads this tick. First: Patricia has restructured to owner-operator and laid off workers. The company is smaller and different now. My role as GM in this new structure is undefined and I need to clarify it directly with her — not by phone, in person, in the next week. Second: Jake Morrison is requesting a meeting and bringing real data. That is exactly what I want from a floor salesperson in a declining market. I accept that meeting and I treat it as a genuine strategic conversation, not a subordinate check-in. Third: Angela's workforce vulnerability map is nearly complete. That document will define who stays and who goes. I need to be in alignment with Angela on how GM-level staff and floor staff are being classified before the map goes final.

chosen_actions.description: Request an in-person sit-down with Patricia Hawkins in her new owner-operator capacity within the next 5 business days. The agenda is explicit: what is my role in the restructured organization, what authority do I retain over the Millfield location, and is there a formal Q2 operational plan she wants me to execute. I go in having already internalized the numbers — service lane at 79%, showroom down, conversion rates off — and I do not pretend any of this is recoverable without a deliberate pivot. I also raise the $12k stay bonus Jake mentioned: I want to know if that program exists, whether it applies to floor sales staff, and whether I have any role in administering it.

Accept Jake Morrison's request for a one-on-one this week. I review whatever data he brings — 90-day close numbers, pipeline by price tier, inventory segment read — without defensiveness. I answer his question about the stay bonus honestly: I have heard the $12k figure mentioned but I do not have confirmed details yet, and I tell him I am raising it directly with Patricia this week. I do not categorize him or his future before Angela's map is done. I treat this as the conversation of two people trying to hold something together.

Send Angela Wright a brief message acknowledging that her vulnerability map is near completion and asking for a heads-up before it goes to Patricia — specifically, whether GM-tier staff at the store level are included in the classification matrix or treated as a separate category. I am not trying to influence the methodology. I am trying to know where I stand before I find out in a meeting with my boss.

Write a private note — not a report, not a memo — about each person who was laid off this month. What their role was. What they contributed. Who I can call on their behalf: Howard Liu at the parts store, any service contacts who might have openings, Angela's transition program. This is not about managing my image. It is about the fact that some of these people have been on this floor since before I was GM, and I was the one signing off on the staffing decisions that made their positions vulnerable.

response.inner_monologue: I walked into Patricia's office last tick with clean numbers and made the case for the service lane. Now she is an owner-operator and people are gone and I do not know if that case landed or if it got buried in the restructuring. I have been in this business since I was washing cars at 19. I know how to read a floor, I know how to hold a team together, and I know what a dying showroom smells like. The question I cannot answer yet is whether any of that matters in the organization Patricia is building now. I need to get in front of her and find out — because managing this floor blind for another month is not something I am willing to do.
